groups.title: Supplementation foundation
groups.proposal: Build supplementation from two complete nuclear clauses while preserving the affixal personal pronoun as head and the added clause as supplement.
groups.writingJob: Compose two owner-issued complete clauses without replacing the principal personal-pronoun head, and distinguish shared from included reference only when that meaning is genuinely unresolved.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to recognize the principal, its personal-pronoun head, and the added supplementary clause rather than reading the supplement as an English-style replacement subject.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the two clauses, chooses their principal-supplement relation, and chooses shared or included reference only when both are possible; the application preserves clause completeness and head status.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Clause composition, captured principal and adjoined Results, and the conditional reference-mode choice; do not expose head status or clause completeness as choices.

groups.title: Shared supplementary subjects and have
groups.proposal: Bind the supplementary NNC subject to the principal subject by real referent identity and derive the locative ca-h plus possessive-NNC have interpretation automatically.
groups.writingJob: Require a real shared referent between the supplementary subject and principal subject, keep person-number agreement as evidence rather than identity, and recognize the licensed locative have construction without inventing a have verb.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through supplementary-subject emphasis and the literal locative-plus-possessive structure behind English have translations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses shared subject supplementation when another role is possible; the application validates referent identity and derives the have interpretation from the entered clause structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse conditional head-role choice; do not add a have control or an agreement control.

groups.title: Shared supplementary objects and possessors
groups.proposal: Bind the supplement subject to a licensed principal object or possessor and block an English-style direct possessor-as-modifier analysis.
groups.writingJob: Expose object or possessor only when the typed principal licenses it, unify the selected head with the supplementary subject, and reject structurally impossible head roles.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to identify supplementary objects and possessors through their personal-pronoun cross-reference rather than English word order.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses object or possessor only when both readings are structurally possible; otherwise the application derives the only licensed role.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the conditional head-role choice and hide impossible roles; do not add a general object or possessor switch.

groups.title: Recursive supplementation
groups.proposal: Build an acyclic hierarchy in which a supplement can itself be principal to another supplement.
groups.writingJob: Compose repeated supplementation through typed continuation frames while preserving each complete clause and every reference link.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through nested possession and reference chains from the outer principal through each supplement.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses which completed composition is reused as principal or supplement; the application validates the acyclic hierarchy.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the existing composition recapture actions; do not expose recursion depth as a number control.

groups.title: Reference contact, demonstratives, and ambiguity
groups.proposal: Treat personal-pronoun referent identity as the contact, license demonstrative NNC supplements, and preserve real third-person subject-object ambiguity.
groups.writingJob: Unify referents rather than stems, accept owner-issued demonstrative NNCs as supplements, and retain all licensed third-person contact roles until the user selects an intended reading.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through indefinite-specific contact, demonstrative supplementation, traditional fused spelling, and third-person ambiguity.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses among genuine contact readings; the application derives available roles and spelling projections from typed clauses.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse conditional role choices; do not infer a role from stem identity, word order, or traditional fused spelling.

groups.title: Topic and comment
groups.proposal: Derive topic-comment structure from a preposed supplement while keeping syntactic role separate from order.
groups.writingJob: Linearize principal and supplement in either licensed order, derive topic only for supplement-first order, allow emphatic ca on the comment, and preserve nested topics and unresolved principal ambiguity.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to separate topic order from subject, object, possessor, and principal status.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses order and resolves real principal ambiguity; the application derives topic, comment, and emphatic-ca placement.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse clause order, principal selection, and licensed particle capture; do not make topic a separate checkbox.

groups.title: Information questions by supplementation
groups.proposal: Form an entity information question by replacing the supplement with an initial interrogative pronominal NNC while preserving its head link.
groups.writingJob: Require an owner-issued interrogative NNC supplement, place it sentence-initially, preserve its selected head binding, and realize question punctuation.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader to recover which supplement was replaced and therefore what entity the question asks about.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended interrogative source and head relation; the application enforces initial placement and question realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse interrogative source, head role, and sentence controls; do not add a separate movement control.
